title: Current externalized workaround first — logistics post-provider residual
purpose: Move beyond internal hiring. Bind named current Xuzhou/Jiangsu private actors that already have commercial relationships with external logistics providers while still paying an internal control layer to compare providers, manage contracts, monitor execution, resolve exceptions and switch weak suppliers. Then test whether that post-provider residual is genuine whitespace or an already-mature control-plane category.
scan_rule: EXTERNALIZED EXECUTION + INTERNAL CONTROL LAYER = REAL POST-PROVIDER RESIDUAL
MANAGING MULTIPLE 3PLS IS ALREADY A 4PL / CONTROL-TOWER FUNCTION
Retain nothing until the residual survives mature 4PL, control-tower, TMS and integrated-logistics routes.

post_incumbent_test.question: Do the named actors still have an observed missing edge after current 4PL, control-tower, TMS and integrated logistics routes are considered?
known: The named actors already use external execution providers and still retain an internal coordination / exception / governance layer.
The residual is therefore more real than a purely internal-hiring pattern.
unknown: Whether the named actors have tried an integrated 4PL/control-tower provider.
Why an existing control-tower or integrated-logistics route cannot replace or materially reduce the internal control layer.
Whether the remaining responsibility requires internal authority, shipment-specific technical judgment, customer ownership or another non-externalizable function.
Whether a new entrant could win economically against mature integrated logistics providers.

material_learning: Scan 026 directly observes a post-provider residual for the first time: outsourced logistics execution does not eliminate the buyer's internal coordination, governance and exception burden.
That residual is economically real because companies maintain internal roles over commercial freight-forwarder/carrier/logistics-supplier relationships.

The generic residual is not whitespace: 4PL, control towers, TMS and integrated logistics providers already productize multi-provider orchestration, visibility, cost/lead-time optimization and exception handling.
The remaining unknown is adoption/access fit at the named companies, not whether the generic category exists.
A new Rooter layer cannot be promoted merely because a firm still employs a logistics coordinator.
cross_industry_result.current_best_next_truth: Fresh Scan 027 should preserve CURRENT EXTERNALIZED WORKAROUND FIRST but exclude mature procurement and logistics-control categories. Search current named Xuzhou/Jiangsu private actors already paying external service providers in a less mature responsibility function while still carrying duplicated internal coordination, provider switching or unresolved exceptions. Retain only if no mature aggregation/control-plane incumbent already owns the residual.
